title: Harden sshd: localhost bind, key before listen
head: de72071bdc87
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Changed shell test fails on this head, and running it unmodified would execute a real host-key generator
leads.consequence: The -T stub prints only password settings, so the new loopback check always removes 20-omarchy-localhost.conf and exits 1 in the first success case. The sudo stub's fallback executes ssh-keygen -A without remapping any /etc/ssh output; if the test process has write access to /etc/ssh and host keys are missing, it can create host keys there. A safely isolated run replacing only the -A call exits 1; when the stub also prints real OpenSSH-style loopback lines it exits 0. Add an -A stub and an -T listener dump before claiming the test passes.

leads.summary: Loopback validator accepts additional remote listeners
leads.consequence: A preexisting ListenAddress 0.0.0.0:22 or [::]:22 is additive in OpenSSH. -T reports that address along with both loopback addresses, yet the two grep existence tests succeed and emit 'Localhost bind only.' The script can enable sshd with remote listeners; an already open UFW rule or disabled firewall makes them reachable. A positive-control stub that includes the extra wildcard line still passes all six shell test cases. Require every effective listener to belong to the allowed loopback set, not just the existence of two lines.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F3 extra-listener case (in draft)

leads.summary: A rejected bind drop-in is silently downgraded to unrestricted listening
leads.consequence: With an existing AddressFamily inet, the ::1 ListenAddress cannot resolve under AF_INET, so -t rejects the new file. The handler removes it and returns 0, the later hardening -t/-T can pass without it, and start_sshd enables sshd using the remaining default or administrator ListenAddress. It prints an initial error but then a success and ssh $USER@hostname; when ufw exists open_firewall additionally prints 'SSH firewall port left closed (localhost bind only)' despite no bind, and if a prior firewall allow rule exists remote listening resumes. Unlike -T failure, this branch does not abort. Fail closed or explicitly distinguish policy unsupported from success.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F3 AddressFamily case (in draft)

leads.summary: Failed re-run deletes an existing previously valid loopback binding
leads.consequence: On re-run, install overwrites the existing 20-omarchy-localhost.conf before checking. A failing -T or the later hardening check unconditionally removes that file, rather than restoring its prior contents. For an active service the current listener is not reloaded on these errors, but at its next restart it can take default/administrator listeners; a previously open firewall rule leaves it externally reachable. The command exits 1 (except the soft -t branch H3), so the operator may believe no change persisted. Preserve and restore an existing file on every failed path.

leads.summary: Validation can disable passwords and start sshd even when its authorized-key path is not usable
leads.consequence: A prior administrator config such as AuthorizedKeysFile none (without a separate AuthorizedKeysCommand) or PubkeyAuthentication no is valid to sshd -t/-T. The command still writes its key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, checks only passwordauthentication and kbdinteractiveauthentication in -T, starts sshd, and claims authorized keys work. In that configuration the imported key is never accepted and password authentication has been disabled; a remote operator has no login by the advertised method. Inspect the applicable key-auth and user-specific configuration before hardening, or report inability to prove key login.
leads.triage: dropped: key-usability checks absent at base too (pre-existing, not caused by PR); addressed by open #9506

leads.summary: Writable home directory allows a success message with no working authorized-key login
leads.consequence: Under OpenSSH's default StrictModes yes, a group- or world-writable $HOME makes sshd ignore the authorized_keys entry even though the script tightens .ssh and the file. The command disables passwords and starts sshd with no usable login via the key it installed. This is already guarded in migrations/1788124236.sh:78-85 and proposed independently in open #9506, but not in this setup command. Test user home modes/ownership before disabling passwords.

leads.summary: CLI metadata still promises to open the firewall
leads.consequence: omarchy commands --all --json and omarchy setup security sshd --help consume the stale summary 'open the firewall' from the executable header, but open_firewall only prints a manual suggestion and intentionally does not run ufw. Callers relying on the discovery API receive incorrect behavior. Update the metadata summary to 'leave the SSH firewall port closed' or equivalent.

leads.summary: SSH removal leaves the new localhost bind drop-in behind
leads.consequence: Removal disables the service and clears its UFW rate-limit rule but never removes 20-omarchy-localhost.conf. If an administrator later re-enables sshd directly, its listener remains loopback-only despite the supposedly removed setup; reinstalling OpenSSH also does not clear an unowned file in /etc. Clarify whether this policy intentionally survives removal, or clean it up in the matching remove flow; also consider the retained 10-omarchy-hardening.conf.

leads.summary: Documented SSH/firewall acceptance contract is still out of sync
leads.consequence: The manual promises the SSH menu opens UFW 22, and the opt-in installed-system acceptance test explicitly requires a '22/tcp LIMIT' entry after calling this script. The changed script deliberately never adds that rule, so on a normal closed-port install the acceptance test fails and users following the manual cannot connect remotely; manual/51-unattended-installs.md:27 describes a separate installer path and was not assumed to call this script. Align the manual and installed-system acceptance test with whichever reachability policy is intended.

leads.summary: Five unstacked SSH PRs need explicit integration; one downstream fixture cannot pass against this head
leads.consequence: Read-only compare API reports diverged for #9043, #9506, #9307, #9463 and #9474 relative to #12099. Three-way merges using each PR's own base report script conflicts for #9043 (2), #9307 (1), #9463 (4), #9474 (4), and a test conflict for #9506 (1). In particular #9043's new pkexec-key fixture has a sudo stub that always exits 0 and does not print -T listeners; even if the script conflict is resolved preserving this head's validation, its test will exit before its expected 'sudo:systemctl enable --now sshd.service'. Reconcile these branches and repair fixtures before combining them; #9506 production script merges cleanly and its home-mode guard works (plan-9506 run), but its test has a conflict; #9474 itself contains #9463, but neither is stacked with #12099.
leads.triage: corroborates F7; #9043 extra conflict not published (already conflicts with quattro per Opus)

leads.summary: Missing UFW suppresses even the remote-access recovery hint
leads.consequence: If ufw is not installed, omarchy-cmd-missing returns success, open_firewall returns immediately and prints no notice. Nevertheless 20-omarchy-localhost.conf remains, and the closing message advertises ssh $USER@hostname, which is unreachable from other machines. Always print the loopback caveat and conditional firewall instructions rather than hiding both when ufw is absent.

limits: No native sshd invocation was made. The -t rejection and listener-addition cases were traced in OpenSSH V_10_5_P1 source; runs use sshd stubs, without opening a network listener.

No live install or acceptance VM was reserved. The acceptance failure is conditioned on UFW not already carrying 22/tcp LIMIT; this is the stock closed-port posture in install/config/firewall.sh:2-54.
Run receipts contain suppressed -A host-key generation only; running the unchanged test without the stub would violate the review's write-target boundary even if /etc/ssh happened to be read-only.

flags.claim: the command can still report a loopback-only server while sshd listens on all addresses
Run as root, for example in a container, it would create real host keys on the machine running the test.
Cases for missing host keys, an extra listener, a hardening failure that removes 20-, and SSHD_ACTIVE=1 would cover the new paths.
although ufw still blocks port 22 on a stock setup

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12099#issuecomment-5856544131) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12099#issuecomment-5857410459), checked at head `de72071b`.

**Outcome:** two earlier findings are resolved and the other five remain. The new `sshd -T` check confirms that the loopback addresses are present, but it does not detect other listeners. Two new findings: the unchanged repository test now fails at this head, and a failed re-run removes an earlier run's loopback drop-in.

| Earlier finding | Status at `de72071b` |
|---|---|
| Setup fails when sshd has never started | Resolved |
| A failed re-run leaves the loopback drop-in | Resolved (one new edge case below) |
| "Localhost bind only" printed without being checked | Still present |
| Loopback-only default vs. the rest of the repository | Unchanged |
| Key validation before `install_openssh` | Unchanged |
| Test gaps shown by mutants | Unchanged, see the new test finding |
| Overlapping open PRs #9463, #9474, #9307, #9506 | Unchanged: all still open and still conflicting |

**Verified:**
- **Host keys before the first check.** `sudo ssh-keygen -A` now runs after the install and before the first `sshd -t`. With real OpenSSH 10.5p1 and no host keys, the head exits 0 and ends with listeners on `127.0.0.1:22` and `[::1]:22` only, with the hardening drop-in in place. The previous head exited 1 in the same scenario. `ssh-keygen -A` is the same command Arch's `sshdgenkeys.service` runs.
- **Cleanup after a failed hardening step.** When `disable_password_auth` fails, the `20-` drop-in is now removed. On a re-run against an active server with an administrator `PasswordAuthentication yes`, the head exits 1 with no `20-` file and no reload. The previous head left the file behind.

Of the author's three reply points, host-key generation and drop-in removal hold as described. The `ListenAddress` check is covered in the next section.

### The listener check tests presence, not exclusivity

`bind_localhost` now requires one `ListenAddress` line for `127.0.0.1` and one for `::1` in `sshd -T` output, then prints "Localhost bind only." It never rejects other addresses. OpenSSH accumulates `ListenAddress` entries, so an existing administrator entry stays active next to the new ones:

```text
existing admin setting          head output             effective listeners (sshd -T)
ListenAddress 0.0.0.0           "Localhost bind only."  0.0.0.0:22, 127.0.0.1:22, [::1]:22
ListenAddress ::                "Localhost bind only."  127.0.0.1:22, [::1]:22, [::]:22
AddressFamily inet              drop-in rejected,       0.0.0.0:22
                                removed, exit 0
```

In the `AddressFamily inet` row, `sshd -t` rejects `ListenAddress ::1`. Because of the "keep soft reject" commit, the script removes the drop-in and continues. It then prints "SSH firewall port left closed (localhost bind only)" and "Perfect!". The new check never runs on this path. When ufw is absent, no firewall line is printed at all, as at the previous head.

**Impact:** the command can still report a loopback-only server while sshd also listens on non-loopback addresses. The red "sshd is not listening on loopback only" message describes a check the code does not perform.

**Suggested change:** reject any listener that is not loopback. For example, fail when the following filter is non-empty (tested only on captured `sshd -T` output, not inside the script):

```bash
grep -Ei '^listenaddress[[:space:]]' <<<"$effective_config" |
  grep -Eiv '^listenaddress[[:space:]]+(127\.0\.0\.1|\[::1\]):[0-9]+$'
```

It is empty for the stock, fresh-install and `Port 2222` cases, and it returns the extra line in the `0.0.0.0` and `::` cases. Also consider making the `sshd -t` rejection a failure, or at least not printing "localhost bind only" after the drop-in has been removed.

### The repository test fails at this head and runs the real `ssh-keygen -A`

`bash test/shell.d/setup-security-sshd-test.sh` (unchanged since the earlier review) exits 1 at `de72071b` on its first case, with no `ok` lines. Its `sshd -T` stub prints only the password settings, so the new listener check fails and the script exits. The PR's test plan still marks this test as passing.

The test's `sudo` stub also passes unknown commands to `exec "$@"`, so the new `sudo ssh-keygen -A` runs the real binary against `/etc/ssh`. In a read-only sandbox this printed four "Could not save your private key in /etc/ssh/..." errors. Run as root where host keys are missing, for example in a container, it would create them in that machine's `/etc/ssh` (inferred from source, not run).

**Impact:** the shell suite fails on this branch. Running it can also touch system host keys.

**Suggested change:** add `ListenAddress 127.0.0.1:22` and `ListenAddress [::1]:22` to the `-T)` branch of the `sshd` stub, and add an `ssh-keygen)` case to the `sudo` stub that logs the call instead of running it. With these two changes all 6 checks pass. However, mutants that remove `ensure_host_keys`, remove the `20-` cleanup, disable the listener check, or start sshd before key generation also pass all 6. Cases for missing host keys (key generation before the first `sshd -t`), an extra listener in `-T` output, a hardening failure that removes `20-`, `sshd -t` rejecting only the bind drop-in, a failing `sshd -T`, and `SSHD_ACTIVE=1` would cover the new paths.

### A failed re-run now also removes an earlier run's loopback drop-in

The new cleanup deletes `20-omarchy-localhost.conf` whether or not this run created it. Test setup: a machine already configured by an earlier run, with sshd active, and an administrator then adding `PasswordAuthentication yes`. A re-run prints "Localhost bind only.", then fails hardening and exits 1. It removes both Omarchy drop-ins without mentioning the bind file. The next restart (a reboot, or the openssh upgrade hook) listens on `0.0.0.0:22` and `[::]:22`.

**Impact:** a failed repair silently widens the listener that an earlier successful run had set, although on a stock setup ufw still blocks port 22 unless it was opened earlier.

**Suggested change:** record whether the `20-` file existed before writing it, and on failure restore the previous content instead of deleting it.

**Note:** `ssh-keygen -A` exits 0 even when it cannot write keys, for example on a read-only `/etc/ssh`. `ensure_host_keys` therefore cannot detect the failure, and the later messages blame the drop-ins. This is rare, and the script still exits 1.

**Unchanged findings:** the loopback default still conflicts with the summary line ("open the firewall"), the success message, `manual/35-networking.md`, `manual/48-security.md`, the `22/tcp LIMIT` assertion in `test/acceptance.d/security-test.sh`, `bin/omarchy-remove-security-sshd`, `plans/server.md` and `migrations/1788124236.sh`. "Fixes #8248" still covers only this opt-in command. Key validation still runs before `install_openssh`. The details in the earlier review still apply.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** head `de72071b`, with both changed files unchanged on the current upstream `quattro` branch. The head, previous head (`89e20be1`) and base scripts were run end to end with real OpenSSH 10.5p1 `sshd -t`/`-T` and `ssh-keygen -A` against private config trees. Also run: the repository shell test at each revision, a patched test and test mutants. Everything ran in an isolated sandbox, with privileged, systemd, package and firewall commands stubbed and the host-key generation of Arch's `sshd.service` modelled. No VM, real systemd or network listeners. The acceptance test and omarchy-iso harness were read, not run, and IPv6-disabled kernels were assessed from source only.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
